title: Grand XOR Counting Problem Challenge II
statementMd:
The annual GXCPC (Grand XOR Counting Problem Challenge) is here again! This year, Judge Colin has prepared another super difficult counting problem for the contestants! Can you slay this ultimate counting problem and win the championship?

Eva has two magic parameters 𝑘1k1 and 𝑘2k2.

Colin has two integer sequences 𝑎1,𝑎2,⋯,𝑎𝑛a1,a2,⋯,an and 𝑏1,𝑏2,⋯,𝑏𝑛b1,b2,⋯,bn.

They want to know how many pairs of indices (𝑖,𝑗)(i,j) satisfy:

- 1≤𝑖<𝑗≤𝑛1≤i<j≤n
- 𝑘1⊕𝑎𝑖⊕𝑎𝑗<𝑘2⊕𝑏𝑖⊕𝑏𝑗k1⊕ai⊕aj<k2⊕bi⊕bj

Where ⊕⊕ represents the bitwise XOR operation.

## Input

The first line contains three integers 𝑛,𝑘1,𝑘2 (1≤𝑛≤2×105,1≤𝑘1,𝑘2<230)n,k1,k2 (1≤n≤2×105,1≤k1,k2<230), representing the length of the two sequences and the magic parameters.

The second line contains 𝑛n integers 𝑎1,𝑎2,⋯,𝑎𝑛 (1≤𝑎𝑖<230)a1,a2,⋯,an (1≤ai<230), representing the first sequence.

The third line contains 𝑛n integers 𝑏1,𝑏2,⋯,𝑏𝑛 (1≤𝑏𝑖<230)b1,b2,⋯,bn (1≤bi<230), representing the second sequence.

## Output

A single integer, representing the number of pairs satisfying the condition.

## Note

There are two valid pairs in the sample: (2,3)(2,3) and (4,5)(4,5)
